Hi Chau, nice work. I have a few comments.
Please prefix the symbol with `LIBPLDM_`
Done
What is this required for?
Done
Do library consumers need to use these values? My feeling is they're only needed by the library implementation.

Table 16 Section 9.7 in DSP0242 v1.0.0 mentions these as

> PLDM completion codes for file transfer that are beyond the scope of PLDM_BASE_CODES in DSP0240

I think callers of DfOpen() would need these to handle each situation correspondingly.
Done

Please consistently apply the `pldm_file_` symbol prefix throughout:

https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/main/docs/checklists/changes.md?plain=1#L114-L116
Done

No packed structs please:

https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/main/docs/checklists/changes.md?plain=1#L151-L152
Done
What about other errors, such as `-EOVERFLOW` if the provided destination buffer is too short?
Done
Please make sure to mention all error values possible.
Done
I prefer these are tested in the same order as the parameters in the function prototype.
Done
No; please rather define a `std::array` with the expected bytes and compare the payload to the array directly.
Done
I realise existing practice has been to lump these all together, but going forward I rather we split "bad" tests into their own `TEST()` cases.

I split bad test into various cases for this patch and the previous. Invalid memory allocation cases will be in the same function, and invalid input/output length will be in the same function. Please help review.
See above.
Done
